I farm wheat and maize on the same 30 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so this year I will keep the full 30 mu in winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. I am 70, my family has some off-farm work, and I have well irrigation, so I will choose a management style that is steady, familiar, and not too risky. I will use improved wheat seed because it is stable and easy for me to manage, and hybrid maize because maize hybrids usually give me better yield. I will not push fertilizer to the maximum because that raises cost and risk, but I will still feed the crops enough to protect yield on irrigated land. For wheat, I will use moderate nitrogen with balanced phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate a few key times, spray a few times for weeds and disease if needed, and use rotary tillage because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize quickly on the same land, keep fertilizer a bit higher on nitrogen for maize, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and keep pesticide use moderate. My goal is stable grain output, manageable labor, and lower production risk rather than chasing the very highest yield.
